heading: Incoming values
body: FromPath reads a path value, such as {id}. FromQuery reads the query string after ?. FromBody reads the JSON request body. FromHeader reads a request header. FromCookie reads a cookie. A marker may name the value, such as FromQuery("page_size"); without a name it uses the parameter name. Each parameter has one marker at most. A method has at most one FromBody parameter, because a request has one body, and a GetRoute method has none, because a GET request has no body; the build refuses both. Python writes the marker inside the type, such as `id: Annotated[int, from_path]`. The identify method of the IdentityProvider class may read a header or a cookie with FromHeader or FromCookie too. One parameter without a marker receives the request in the language's own type, such as a Fetch Request, urllib.request.Request, HttpExchange, HttpRequestMessage, http::Request, a shelf Request or *http.Request; PHP reads $_SERVER, $_GET, $_POST, $_COOKIE and php://input instead. Parameter types validate these values before the method runs. Model return types validate the response. OPTIONS publishes the generated schema. HEAD uses the GET route.
